title: [Shortcut Guide] Default "Hold Windows key" behavior interferes with Win+V and Win+H
summary: The reporter confirmed the existing Shortcut Guide settings are a practical workaround for their case, while noting the hold-key default can still be finicky for accessibility-sensitive workflows.

status.label: Needs team follow-up
status.detail: The author replied after the maintainer workaround guidance. The issue no longer needs the reporter for the same confirmation; it needs a maintainer/product decision on whether the current settings guidance is sufficient or whether defaults/discoverability should change.

next_action.label: Team response needed
next_action.reason: Do not ask the reporter to repeat the confirmation. A maintainer should decide whether to close as handled-by-settings, document the workaround, or keep the issue open for defaults/discoverability/accessibility follow-up.

judgment.rationale: The original reporter identified a practical workaround. A separate report that the guide interrupts Win-key window dragging warrants a focused compatibility check rather than closing as handled by settings.
evidence: The original report describes Win+V and Win+H being disrupted by the default Hold Windows key behavior.
A maintainer explained the existing controls: disable close-on-release, increase hold duration, or turn Hold Windows key off and use the activation shortcut.
The reporter replied on 2026-09-20 that turning Hold Windows key off and using the activation shortcut is likely the more practical option.
A later commenter reports that AltSnap Win-key movement and resizing stop when the guide opens. This is report evidence, not independent runtime confirmation.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare the existing workaround with the default Hold Windows key mode for both built-in shortcuts and Win-key dragging before deciding on defaults or documentation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No code change is selected before isolating whether overlay activation or key release interrupts each interaction.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide Hold Windows key can interfere with built-in Windows shortcuts when the hold timer activates; current settings can mitigate it, but the reporter raised usability/accessibility concerns.
known_information: The report covers PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 on Windows 11 25H2.
The issue affects Shortcut Guide Hold Windows key behavior with Win+V Clipboard History and Win+H Voice typing.
Disabling Hold Windows key avoids the interference.
A maintainer identified existing controls: close-on-release, hold duration, and using the activation shortcut instead.
The reporter identified Hold Windows key Off plus the activation shortcut as their preferred workaround.
inferences: The immediate reporter-actionable question has been answered.
Remaining work is a maintainer/product decision about whether settings guidance is enough or whether defaults/discoverability/accessibility should be improved.
issue_context.analysis: Compare the timing of overlay activation, key release, and focus loss. AltSnap is a separate control from the built-in Win+V/Win+H shortcuts. Existing settings remain useful workarounds and no further reporter response is needed.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all seven comments through the 2026-09-20 reporter reply.
Compared current labels: Needs-Team-Response and Status-Reproducible are present; Needs-Author-Feedback is not present.
Read the later AltSnap report and checked for a PR referencing this issue; no covering PR was found.

actions.label: Compare Win-key shortcuts and dragging across Shortcut Guide modes

prerequisites: Use a test profile with Clipboard History and voice typing available; add AltSnap configured for the Win key only for the third-party control.
steps: With Hold Windows key enabled, try Win+V and Win+H both before and after the guide appears. Record whether key release closes the other interface.
Hold Win and drag or resize a test window with AltSnap past the guide activation threshold. Record when the drag stops, if it does.
Repeat with close-on-release disabled, then with Hold Windows key off and the explicit activation shortcut enabled.
reproduce.expected_result: The comparison identifies which configuration preserves each interaction and whether interruption correlates with overlay display or key release.
